provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The input contains a single 2x2 block of the background-clearing colour (original colour 0, visible colour palette[0]). Every row and every column containing that colour is painted with palette[0], except cells holding the preserved colour (original 2, visible palette[2]). The mechanism is a union of a horizontal band and a vertical band. The set {rows, columns} maps to itself under every D4 transform: rotations swap rows with columns, and reflections only reorder indices. So the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates and needs no direction specialization. Only the two colour roles are specialized, as palette constants. Bands span the full grid width and height, so rectangular grids and blocks touching boundaries are handled naturally.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the only cells with colour palette[0] in the input are the cells of the block, which matches the generator. If the random field contained stray palette[0] cells, their rows and columns would also be cleared, which is the same behaviour as the archived solver. The program does not use the demonstrations. No contradictions between the fixtures and the rule were observed. I have not run any tests.
